title: The Mpemba Effect: Why Hot Water Can Freeze Faster Than Cold
question: How can hot water sometimes freeze before cold water, when the hot water has to cool down through the cold water's starting temperature first?
summary: Under certain conditions, a container of hot water freezes faster than an otherwise identical container of cold water — a counterintuitive result known since antiquity, rediscovered by a Tanzanian schoolboy in 1963, and still not fully explained by physicists today.
